Reject the proposed integration as written. It mixes incompatible APIs, frame-dependent stepping, unsafe ID/event lifetimes, post-solve collision filtering, indiscriminate bullet use, and a rollback claim stronger than Box2D 3.1.1 supports.

- **Source/API drift — pinned fact and policy:** Pin Box2D **v3.1.1**, released 2025-06-04 at commit `8c661469c9507d3ad6fbd2fea3f1aa71669c2fe3`. Treat its tagged public headers as authoritative because the website Doxygen remained at 3.1.0. Record source-tree, public-header, and binary hashes; CMake options; compiler/version; architecture; floating-point flags; task system; and adapter version in a compatibility manifest. Compile a small adapter probe against that exact artifact. Use only 3.x C constructs: `b2Default*Def` initializers, opaque value IDs, shapes, free functions, and `b2World_Step`. Do not use 2.4 C++ bodies/fixtures/listeners or the old iteration-pair `Step` form. APIs from 3.2-era `main`, including snapshot, recording, state-hash, runtime-worker, and additional CCD work, are unavailable in this pin and must not enter the adapter.

- **ID ownership and mutation — adapter contract:** Box2D IDs are generational handles, not durable gameplay identity; their validity protection covers limited allocation churn and does not make them safe to retain indefinitely. Give every world object a stable application ID and keep adapter-owned application-ID-to-Box2D-ID mappings. Normalize creation and destruction into deterministic tick-boundary commands. World destruction invalidates all children; body destruction also destroys attached shapes and joints; chain or body destruction invalidates chain segment IDs. Invalidate the entire affected mapping cascade immediately and make queued gameplay records contain application IDs, never raw Box2D IDs. `b2Shape_IsValid` may prevent invalid access but cannot recover identity. Initialize all definitions with the corresponding `b2DefaultWorldDef`, `b2DefaultBodyDef`, `b2DefaultShapeDef`, or `b2DefaultChainDef`. Account explicitly for `b2DestroyShape(shapeId, updateBodyMass)`, deferred `b2Body_ApplyMassFromShapes`, sensor mass, and the fact that sensor status cannot change after shape creation. Verify this with creation/destruction permutations, chain/body cascades, jointed-lift teardown, destruction-generated events, and allocation churn beyond 64K handles.

- **Step and task phase — shipping policy:** Decouple simulation from the 48–240 Hz renderer. Evaluate fixed 60 Hz and 120 Hz main ticks with substep counts 1, 2, 4, and 8; ship the cheapest row that satisfies the movement, joint, tunneling, and CPU criteria, then freeze both tick and substep count. Do not change substeps because a render frame was slow. Render interpolated completed states; assign inputs and commands to simulation ticks. `b2World_Step` is an exclusive locked phase. Any worker count above serial requires correctly paired `enqueueTask`/`finishTask`, stable worker indices, and application-owned threads. Collision and task callbacks must be bounded and thread-safe, use immutable precomputed context, publish only to bounded thread-local/indexed storage, and neither read nor mutate the world. Join tasks before outside-step queries or mutations. Benchmark fixed worker candidates rather than using hardware concurrency at runtime; freeze the selected worker count in the compatibility manifest.

- **Events and sensors — lifetime contract:** Enable body, contact, sensor, and PreSolve events only where needed because applicable event generation defaults off. After every main step, before another step or gameplay mutation, drain each borrowed event array, copy required scalar data, resolve durable application IDs while mappings still exist, canonicalize by event kind and application IDs, and discard all borrowed/raw Box2D data. Begin/end/contact records are transient observations, not persistent objects; build application-owned overlap and support sets from them. End events can be caused by destruction and can contain destroyed IDs. Emit “landed” only on a canonical support-set transition from empty to nonempty, preventing duplicate landings. Sensors may detect sensors, but have no CCD; fast trigger crossings therefore require a ray/shape-cast policy. Test enter/exit, sensor-sensor, destruction while overlapping, multiple simultaneous contacts, and event-order permutations.

- **Queries and casts — observation contract:** Run queries only outside the locked step and consume their callback data immediately. `b2World_OverlapAABB` returns approximate broadphase candidates; use `b2World_OverlapShape` or narrow-phase geometry for actual overlap. Ray, overlap, and shape-cast callbacks may arrive in arbitrary order, so collect, filter, copy, then sort by fraction and durable application ID. A v3.1.1 cast that starts overlapped can return fraction zero with a zero normal and arbitrary overlap point; treat this as a distinct “starts inside” state, never as a usable surface normal. A downward ray may supplement ledge prediction, but “ray hit or any contact” is not an adequate grounding contract and must never trigger a body teleport.

- **One-way contacts — PreSolve contract:** Register `b2PreSolveFcn` and set `enablePreSolveEvents` only on shapes requiring one-way behavior. Decide before collision resolution; disabling after `b2World_Step` is too late because impulses have already been solved. Contacts re-enable during collision processing, so reject an unwanted contact on every applicable step. The callback must use immutable precomputed data: previous foot position, platform plane/side, relative velocity including platform translation/rotation, approach direction, drop-through state, spawn-overlap handling, and a durable pair identity. Stable v3.1.1 explicitly warns that this PreSolve technique can fail or pause for high-speed collisions, so define a measured speed/thickness limit; outside it, use a predictive cast/custom-mover policy or redesign that platform as solid. Exercise approach from above/below, lateral edge entry, drop-through, spawn overlap, translating and rotating platforms, frame stalls, and fast crossings.

- **Character movement — chosen contract:** Use a solver-driven physical capsule for the initial implementation because the players must interact naturally with moving platforms, jointed lifts, and other dynamic bodies. Drive it through velocity/force policy and solver contacts; never teleport it onto a ray hit. Maintain a canonical support record containing durable support ID, qualified normal, relative vertical velocity, and platform point velocity. Evaluate control in the support’s moving frame so translating or rotating platforms carry the player without fabricating world-space teleports. Rays or short shape casts may provide prediction and ledge information but do not replace support qualification. Keep Box2D’s experimental geometric mover as a separate comparison, not a hybrid: its capsule is outside world ownership, uses `b2World_CollideMover` and `b2World_CastMover`, assembles planes for `b2SolvePlanes`, and clips velocity with `b2ClipVector`; the application would then own slopes, steps, platform motion, pushing, dynamic interaction, events, and replication. Adopt it only if a dedicated prototype beats the physical-body contract on the declared scenarios.

- **CCD and bullets — scoped policy:** Default continuous collision covers dynamic bodies against static bodies. Bullet mode extends a sparse measured body to static, kinematic, and dynamic targets, but not other bullets, and may interfere with joints; therefore do not enable it on every moving body. Classify projectiles: use bullet bodies only when physical response and the measured collision-pair envelope require them; use ray/shape casts for first-hit or fast-trigger semantics. Sensors have no CCD, and continuous-collision contacts may not emit ordinary events until the following step, so document acceptable event latency. Test speed, radius, obstacle thickness, impact angle, target motion/type, substeps, bullet-versus-bullet, and jointed bodies, then enable bullets only for classes that fail without them.

- **Determinism and rollback — bounded claim:** Box2D targets determinism across 64-bit platforms under its prescribed math/build conditions, but that is not a guarantee across arbitrary CPUs, compilers, flags, worker configurations, creation order, or future 3.x releases. Stable v3.1.1 has no public snapshot or rollback API, and player transforms cannot restore hidden contacts, solver state, sleep state, joints, or application state. Do not replay captured render deltas. Reconstruct the exact pinned world and replay a complete, canonically ordered tick history of inputs, spawns, destroys, property changes, controller state, and commands. Hash a durable-ID-sorted semantic projection every tick—not merely final player transforms—and retain the first divergent tick plus structured field differences. Freeze build and worker count for production compatibility unless every additional lane is explicitly qualified; any Box2D update or materially different build is a new simulation version.

**Executable evidence run**

1. Create a release manifest for Windows x64/MSVC and Linux x64/Clang or GCC, including every source, header, binary, build, FP, adapter, and worker detail. Re-run the pinned upstream determinism seed (`dt = 1/60`, four substeps, workers 1–5, expected sleep step 288, expected hash `0x35467e1e`) on each exact artifact; this validates the artifact only, not the game.

2. Run the full matrix of fixed tick `{60,120} Hz`, substeps `{1,2,4,8}`, and fixed worker candidates against representative and worst-case scenes: four players, about 2,000 active shapes, maximum moving/rotating platforms, jointed lifts, sensors, one-way contacts, dense resting contacts, and maximum simultaneous projectiles. Record `b2World_Step` and whole-simulation CPU p50/p95/p99/max, task time/imbalance, solver counters exposed by the pin, active bodies/shapes/contacts, body/sensor/contact event counts, query/cast counts, allocations, and missed-frame/catch-up counts. Require the slowest supported machine’s worst-case `b2World_Step` p99 to remain within the 3 ms budget while all correctness scenarios pass; an average frame time is insufficient.

3. Run adversarial movement and lifetime suites for low render rate, render-rate sweeps, landing once, ledge transitions, support loss, platform translation/rotation/reversal, drop-through, underside approach, spawn overlap, simultaneous supports, joint teardown, sensor destruction, query initial overlap/equal-fraction hits, and ID churn. Capture the first incorrect tick with ordered inputs, commands, events, support set, and relevant body state.

4. Run the projectile envelope across all declared speed/radius/thickness/angle/target combinations for default CCD, bullet, ray cast, and shape cast. Report misses, duplicate hits, event latency, CPU percentiles, and joint disruption. The chosen policy must have no misses inside its published envelope.

5. For replay, use a long canonical recording plus injected late-input rollbacks. Compare every tick across repeated runs, chosen worker count, worker-count candidates, Windows/Linux builds, and supported compiler lanes. Hash all gameplay-relevant bodies, velocities, awake/enabled state, logical joint state, overlaps, support/controller state, and ordered application commands. Publish only the exact lanes and duration that remain divergence-free; preserve the first-divergence artifact for failures. Requalify on every source, compiler, flag, adapter, or worker-policy change.

Keep generic loop/phase ownership in `architecting-real-time-physics`, collision policy in `rigid-body-collision-contact`, lift/joint design in `constraints-ragdolls-active-physics`, controller design in `character-controller-movement`, rollback compatibility in `networked-deterministic-physics`, reproduction in `debugging-testing-physics`, and performance methodology in `profiling-scaling-physics`.
